title: CrowdFlow AI
discipline: Data analysis / Agent simulation / Interaction design
summary: A research prototype connecting pedestrian trajectories, social-force simulation and entrance layouts to study how crowds move through public events.
short: Reading pedestrian movement. Testing the spaces that shape it.
takeaway: Crowd movement becomes a design question when trajectories, spatial conditions and simulation can be read together.
coverAlt: Flow lines showing pedestrian movement in the CrowdFlow AI analysis
mediaCaption: Selected trajectories from one TopView 1A recording. Observed movement, rather than a calibrated simulation.

sections.title: Question / Where does a crowd become a bottleneck?
paragraphs: An event entrance brings arrival patterns, screening capacity and limited queueing space into one small area. Starting with data from Lyon's Festival of Lights, CrowdFlow AI investigates where people gather, when movement slows and how an entrance layout might change those conditions.
The aim is to make a planning question tangible: which gates, barriers and paths deserve closer attention before a layout is put into use?

sections.title: Method / Connect observation with adjustable scenarios
paragraphs: CCTV trajectories and recorded contact events are processed into time-based summaries, relative observed density and directional flow maps. A social-force model then provides an adjustable simulation with controls for pedestrian count, gate width, barrier length and duration.

A Streamlit interface brings evidence, entrance design, scenario comparison and animated flow into one workflow. An optional language-model module produces interpretations of potential bottlenecks and suggestions for further exploration.

sections.title: What exists / A working environment for spatial comparison
paragraphs: The prototype includes data-processing scripts, a configurable simulation, an interactive dashboard and generated analysis images. Multi-gate presets explore equal-width entrances and a wider central gate through simulated throughput, queue-area density, average speed and potential contacts.
Heat maps and trajectory views help locate the spatial patterns behind those values. Together, the outputs create a way to inspect a scenario and ask more precise questions about its behavior.

sections.title: Next questions / What makes a comparison reliable?
paragraphs: The current scenarios are exploratory: total entrance width and random starting conditions are not fully matched, and simulated potential contacts are not equivalent to recorded sensor events. The prototype therefore does not establish a measured improvement in crowd safety or flow.

The next step is to verify trajectory parsing, align metric definitions and compare layouts under controlled conditions. Repeated runs and parameter calibration would make the differences between layouts more interpretable.

title: GR00T × Isaac Sim
englishTitle: From robot policy to a testable system.
summary: An engineering study of the path from robot demonstrations to policy inference and Isaac Sim control, developed from an open-source GR00T tutorial.
short: Building the interfaces between observation, policy and action.
takeaway: Before a robot policy can be evaluated, its data, observations and actions need a shared, inspectable contract.
deliverables: 12 passing CPU protocol and validation tests
coverAlt: Diagram connecting data preparation, a GR00T policy service and Isaac Sim
mediaCaption: The engineering workflow links dataset checks, policy serving and simulation control.

sections.title: Question / What does it take to connect a policy to a robot?
paragraphs: A robot-learning tutorial spans several systems: demonstrations, model training, inference services and a simulated robot. This project starts from donghoYee's Isaac Sim with GR00T Tutorial and examines the interfaces that connect those systems.

The upstream tutorial targets GR00T N1.5. The immediate objective is a clearer engineering workflow with explicit configurations and checks, establishing the groundwork for later experiments with compatible software, data and scene assets.

sections.title: Method / Define the contract from observation to action
paragraphs: Training requires a LeRobot-compatible dataset and a matching robot configuration. At runtime, camera images, robot state and a task instruction must reach the policy service; its returned actions must then map correctly to the simulated robot's joints.

The engineering work separates these concerns through configuration management, preflight checks and an explicit observation-action protocol. This makes each connection possible to inspect before attempting a full simulation run.

sections.title: What exists / An interface that can be checked in stages
paragraphs: The current package provides a shared HTTP interface for two camera observations, real-policy and mock backends, joint mapping and dataset preflight checks. A mock backend supports protocol debugging before model inference and simulation integration are available.

Twelve CPU protocol and validation tests pass, including failure handling and dual-camera dataset checks. The downloadable engineering package contains the configuration and implementation; real-model inference, GPU training and closed-loop task performance in Isaac Sim remain unverified.

sections.title: Next questions / Does the complete loop work?
paragraphs: The next stage is to fix software and model versions, prepare matching demonstrations and scene assets, and run the complete observation-policy-action loop. Training configuration, inference latency, task outcomes and failure cases should be recorded together.
These experiments are still pending. The current engineering checks demonstrate protocol behavior, rather than a robot task success rate or validated autonomous manipulation.

title: Sunken Plaza
englishTitle: Reading public space through everyday movement.
discipline: Field observation / Spatial reconstruction / Behavioral mapping
summary: An observational study of a campus sunken plaza, using site footage, 3D reconstruction and pedestrian visualization to examine the relationship between movement, pause and public space.
short: Tracing the paths people choose and the places they stay.
takeaway: Everyday routes and pauses offer a way to question how a public space is arranged, connected and sheltered.
coverAlt: A reconstructed sunken plaza with pedestrian trajectories and gathering areas
mediaCaption: Site footage, reconstructed geometry and pedestrian traces form a shared spatial context.

sections.title: Question / How do people make use of an everyday plaza?
paragraphs: The sunken plaza and adjacent campus shop at Tongji University's Siping Road campus accommodate passing through, resting, gathering and children's activities. Changes in level, entrances, seating and shade bring these uses into close proximity.
The group study asks three linked questions: which routes people choose, where movement and lingering concentrate, and how resting facilities and environmental conditions relate to those patterns.

sections.title: Method / Place observation inside a spatial model
paragraphs: Fixed-camera footage captures pedestrian activity, while photographs around the buildings support reconstruction in COLMAP. The geometry is scaled and aligned in Rhino, bringing the site plan, buildings and observed pedestrian positions into a common setting.

Grasshopper files and presentation footage document the making of trajectories, heat maps and animated flows. Reviewing the original video alongside the 3D views helps check how the observed activity is represented.

sections.title: What exists / A visual account of routes and pauses
paragraphs: The sampled footage shows people crossing the lawn, resting on steps and gathering near the shop. The study uses those observations to examine path connectivity and the relationship between entrance circulation and places to stay.

Differences in the use of seating and shade also suggest questions about comfort. Additional paths, clearer activity boundaries and more shelter are proposed design directions, with further observation needed to assess their value.

sections.title: Next questions / Which patterns persist beyond the sample?
paragraphs: The findings describe exploratory observations from the recorded periods. Gaps in sampling, building detail, pedestrian projection and animation continuity limit how confidently the results can be generalized.

Further work would add continuous samples, check the alignment between observed positions and the model, and use consistent definitions for trajectories and heat maps. That would support a more reliable comparison of how the plaza is used over time.
